title: Toffee apples
subtitle: Classic fairground toffee apples with a hard, brittle red sugar shell
excerpt: A toffee apple is an eating apple on a stick coated in hard-crack stage sugar syrup coloured red with food colouring. The syrup must reach 150 degrees Celsius precisely; under that temperature the shell stays sticky rather than setting hard. Everything needs to be ready before you start: the apples skewered, the tin prepared, and the thermometer in the pan.
sourceNotes: Toffee apples are documented in British fairground food from the Victorian era and became particularly associated with Halloween and Guy Fawkes Night. The technique depends on the hard-crack sugar stage (150 degrees Celsius), standard confectionery knowledge documented in sugar-work reference texts.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Toffee apples are best eaten within 2 hours of making. The sugar absorbs moisture from the air and becomes sticky after a few hours. Do not refrigerate.

glossaryTerms.definition: A sugar syrup that has been cooked to between 146 and 155 degrees Celsius. At this temperature virtually all moisture has left the sugar. When the syrup hits cold water it shatters into brittle, glass-like threads. On a toffee apple, hard-crack stage produces the characteristic shell that snaps cleanly when bitten. Below 140 degrees Celsius the sugar stays pliable; below 130 degrees it is sticky.

. A candy thermometer is not optional; judging the temperature by eye is unreliable. Have the apples skewered and the baking paper laid out before you start cooking the syrup.

Sugar syrup at hard-crack stage is around 150 degrees Celsius, roughly three times hotter than boiling water, and sticks to skin. Keep children away from the pan and have cold running water accessible while you work. Do not stir the syrup after it starts boiling.

items.prepNote: small to medium, stalks removed, dried thoroughly with a cloth

content.text: The apples must be completely dry or the toffee will not stick. Wipe each one with a clean dry cloth. Push a wooden skewer or lollipop stick into the stalk end of each apple, pushing it in about halfway. Lightly oil a sheet of baking paper and set aside.

Combine the sugar, golden syrup, water, and cream of tartar in a medium, deep saucepan. Stir gently over low heat just until the sugar dissolves, then stop stirring and increase the heat to medium-high.

Clip the candy thermometer to the side of the pan. Cook without stirring until the syrup reaches 150 degrees Celsius. Remove from heat immediately. Add the red food colouring and swirl the pan gently to mix; do not stir.

Working quickly, tilt the pan at a steep angle and dip each apple into the syrup, rotating it to coat evenly. Hold the apple over the pan briefly to let the excess drip off, then place it on the oiled paper. The toffee will set hard within 3 to 4 minutes at room temperature.
